Οὐρβανός, -οῦ, ὁ (Lat. Urbanus), 
Urban: Rom.16.9.†
(AS)

A man living at the time of United Monarchy, first mentioned at 2Sa.11.3; married to Bathsheba (H1339)
Also named: Ourias (Οὐρίας "Uriah" G3774)
§ Uriah or Urijah = "Jehovah (Yahweh) is my light (flame)"
1) Hittite husband of Bathsheba
2) a priest who built king Ahaz' heathen altar
3) a priest who rebuilt Jerusalem's wall

Οὐρίας, -ου, ὁ (Heb. אוּרִיָּה), 
Uriah: Mat.1.6.†
(AS)

Urim = "lights"
stones kept in a pouch on the high-priest's breastplate, used in determining God's decision in certain questions and issues
Also named: dēlos (δῆλος "Urim" G1212)

δῆλος, -η, -ον 
[in LXX for אוּר, etc. ;] 
__1. visible. 
__2. clear to the mind, evident: Mat.26.73 δ. (sc. ἐστίν), before ὅτι, 1Co.15.27, Gal.3.11.†
SYN.: φανερός, with ref. to outward appearance, manifest as opposite to concealed; δ. with ref. to inner perception, evident, known, under­stood. (AS)
